messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?
I need it for a project at my house, and it needs to happen in the next few weeks. I’m not willing to just wait until A is done with it.

I’d like it not to take up space on my pad much longer, though it’s fine for now. I did agree to keep it here, so I feel a bit bad asking—but I rent, and I’d need my landlord’s permission to change what’s kept there. I haven’t asked him yet.
I want to be able to use it for my weekend trips in the next few weeks. I don’t have a strong view on where it’s stored.
Not quite. It’s not just the project timeline—I need to be able to use the trailer myself, rather than have my plans depend on when A is finished.
Yes. I need the freedom to make my own plans with the trailer, and I need to use it in the next few weeks.
Not quite—I do want to be sure I’m allowed to keep it there, but mostly I’d like the trailer out of the way. I just feel a little awkward asking, since I agreed to the arrangement.
Yes, that’s closer. I’d like the pad back, and I should check with my landlord before agreeing to keep it there longer. I still feel a little responsible since I agreed to it.
Mostly. I want the freedom to take it on my trips without having to negotiate every single time.

Option 2 sounds best for not having to coordinate through B, if we can arrange it soon and agree on the cost. Option 1 could work short-term only if I can use the trailer for my project in the next few weeks. Also, my project is hers, not his.

Option 2 sounds best for getting the pad back, though we’d need to work out the cost, and I should check with my landlord before changing what’s kept there. Option 3 doesn’t really work for me if the trailer stays here. Option 1 might be okay as a short transition, but I’d rather it not sit on my pad for weeks.
